Subject: SDK tracing compatibility & joint workshop proposal

Hi Priyom and Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick chat last week. LangBridge's engineering team reviewed Redwood's serving runtime and we think there's a solid opportunity to make our LangBridge SDK emit trace and prompt metadata in a way that maps cleanly to Redwood's trace model.

High-level ask: would Redwood be open to a short technical workshop to align on header conventions, token attribution (prompt vs system vs tool tokens), and a minimal payload shape for trace passthrough so our customers get end-to-end observability?

We sketched a proposal (attached) that demonstrates a few patterns:
- single header for trace-id + span hints
- structured prompt meta (json-lite) for attribution
- optional KV cache keys propagation for model warm-starting

Ravi from PromptSmith is cc'd — they recently integrated your runtime and can share field-level constraints from the marketplace side.

Proposed next step: 60-minute workshop next week. We can bring an annotated draft SOW if alignment looks good.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Gomez
Head of Integrations, LangBridge Labs
elena.g@langbridge.com

Elena —

Appreciate the write-up and the proposal. We're very interested in standardizing how partner SDKs carry trace and prompt attribution into Redwood's runtime. A couple of firm requirements from our side before the workshop:

1) Token attribution format: we need a stable way to mark token origin (system/prompt/tool) for quality billing and attribution. A small JSON blob in a header is fine but it must be size-bounded (we prefer <2KB).
2) Trace continuity: we require a trace-id and span parent hint so our sampling and trace linking works across retries and fallbacks. Header name preference: X-Redwood-Trace (backwards compatible) or TRACE-ID (if we adopt w3c later).
3) Backwards fallback: SDKs must support a graceful fallback when customers route to older Redwood variants that don't accept the new header.
4) Security: payloads must be signed or HMAC'd when carrying customer-identifying metadata. We can accept token-level HMAC with a shared key during the SOW period.

I'll attach a short spec we use internally for partner integrations and bring engineering (Karthik) to the workshop for kernel-level constraints.

Available slots: Wed 2027-03-03 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 2027-03-05 13:00-14:00 PT. Pick one and we'll book a room+recording.

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

Elena / team —

Quick technical notes ahead of the workshop:

- We're aiming to map any SDK-provided attribution into our internal token map. That mapping must include start/end offsets and a short category tag (sys/prompt/tool). Example: {"segments":[{"start":0,"end":42,"tag":"prompt"}]}
- For tracing, we prefer adding an optional "x-redwood-trace-opts" header that includes a small base64-encoded JSON with sampling hints. That keeps the main TRACE-ID header simple.
- KV cache keys: please limit to a short hashed key (32 chars) rather than full prefixes. We can't accept large blobs in headers.
- We'll demo an example flow showing trace continuity across model fallback (A->B). Please have a simple demo app from LangBridge that emits the proposed headers for the meeting.

I'll load the sandbox policy and a short checklist into the shared drive before the call. Priyom — if we confirm Friday slot I'll invite runtime and security.

Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
